title: Bulgaria announces it will stop sending arms to Ukraine
body:
On 9 June 2026, Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said that the new government led by Prime Minister Rumen Radev would not continue sending arms to Ukraine. Speaking at a press conference, he said: "It is time to sit at the negotiating table." Stoyanov argued that the war had become positional and that more weapons would cost lives without changing the battlefield.

Radev, a former president and long-time critic of military aid to Kyiv, won Bulgaria's parliamentary elections on 19 April 2026. Bulgaria provided 13 military aid packages to Ukraine after the full-scale invasion began in 2022.

Ukraine's Foreign Ministry, through spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi, said Kyiv receives no free aid from Bulgaria but continues defense cooperation on a commercial basis. In March 2026, Ukraine had signed a 10-year security agreement with Bulgaria's former government covering joint drone and arms production. The Kyiv Independent published its report on the announcement on 9 June 2026 and updated it the following day. Stoyanov's statement marked a change from the earlier government's policy of supplying arms to Kyiv.
